headline: SITCON holds at 5 (QUIET): exploited OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 and GitHub secret-scanning abuse lead; KEV deadlines 11-10 and 11-11

bullets.text: New since the 02:19 SITREP: two new medium-severity reports, no new critical or high ones, and SITCON stays at 5 (QUIET). The last 7 days scored 0.74x the 90-day average. OpenSSH and GitHub (4 outlets each) remain the only developing situations.

OpenSSH, 4 outlets: CVE-2026-123158 was exploited in the wild hours after disclosure. OpenSSH issued an emergency fix for the flaw, which lets long passwords bypass SSH auth on Alpine Linux and also reaches routers.

GitHub, 4 outlets: hackers are using Artex to scan GitHub repositories for exposed secrets; Microsoft reports threat actors using agentic AI tooling to find and abuse them; Truffle Security launched a program to revoke nearly 1.5 million live secrets.
Network gear: Zyxel fixed a zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 GS1900 switches after an earlier patch failed to block it; D-Link warned of multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 Series switches.

Breaches: Iris Ohyama disclosed a data cloud breach exposing 7.7 million customers; a $133 million French bank heist ran via a service provider; Chainalysis says credentials for all customers were exposed; DigiCert and WorkOS also reported breaches.

actions: Patch OpenSSH on every internet-facing host for CVE-2026-123158, prioritising Alpine Linux and routers; restrict SSH exposure and review auth logs.
Scan GitHub repos and their history for committed secrets; revoke and rotate anything found and enable secret scanning with push protection.
Clear this week's KEV items today: Adobe Commerce/Magento and Brotli (due 11-10), VMware ESX (11-11), Ivanti Connect Secure (11-13).
Zyxel GS1900 and D-Link DGS-3130 owners: apply the vendors' latest fixes or mitigations and check switches for signs of compromise.
SonicWall SSL-VPN users: patch CVE-2026-19868 (KEV due 2026-11-20) and review VPN logs for logins that skipped MFA.
Iris Ohyama, Chainalysis, DigiCert and WorkOS customers: reset passwords, rotate API keys and credentials, and watch for phishing.
